page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 12 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key characteristic of this server is its bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is weak, falling in the bottom 25% with a score of 1102.49, and single-threaded gzip compression is poor at 18.96 GB/sec. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance reaches an average level of 8789.97. Memory bandwidth tests show average results, with read-only small block cached speeds at 488.85 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 47.08 GB/sec. Passmark memory performance is weak, scoring 1685.71, while database operations and Redis SET operations at 8.27 million operations per second maintain average tier performance.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.3xlarge is its reliance on high-capacity HDD local storage rather than SSDs, which offers massive storage density but limits sequential and random I/O speeds compared to solid-state alternatives. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server provides a high volume of local storage per unit of compute, making it suitable for cold data storage, large-scale data archiving, and distributed file systems. It is also applicable for multi-threaded batch processing and database operations that do not require high-speed SSD performance, though it is less suitable for single-threaded or memory-intensive workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is an x86_64 server featuring 12 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU cores running at 2.5 GHz, 48.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 35,433 GB of bundled local HDD storage. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show weak single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 25%, but average multi-core performance at 8789.97. Memory bandwidth is average, though the Passmark memory score is weak at 1685.71. The server's high storage-to-compute ratio makes it qualitatively cost-effective for storage-dense workloads. It is best suited for distributed file systems, data archiving, and offline multi-threaded batch processing where massive local HDD capacity is required, rather than high-speed I/O or single-threaded compute tasks.
